paragraphs: Bath and North East Somerset Council runs its own fostering service for children from Bath, Keynsham and the rest of the district, and independent agencies such as the services shown above also care for children from the area. The council's current information pack says around 150 children are in foster care locally and that there are not enough approved carers offering the different kinds of care they need.

Those kinds range widely: short-term care of up to about two years, long-term homes, emergency care at night or at weekends, stays of a few days to two weeks, parent and child placements, Family Link short breaks for disabled children, and supported lodgings for young people aged 16 to 25.

To apply you need to be over 21 with a spare bedroom for a child; you do not have to own your home, and working outside the home may be possible. Homes fostering under-fives must be smoke-free. The assessment takes four to six months. Once approved, carers have a supervising social worker, a buddy for the first year, an out-of-hours phone line, support groups, a psychologist who works with foster carers and at least four training events a year. In 2025 the council set up its first Mockingbird constellation, a group of ten foster families supported by a hub home carer.

Our Bath and North East Somerset allowance page sets out the council's published scale: a weekly allowance from £198.17 for children under five to £320.29 for 16 to 18-year-olds, plus a weekly tier payment that starts at £209.96 for every new carer and rises to £287.08 with training. Parent and child placements are paid at £964.08 a week.
Talk to the council and two or three of the services above, and ask each about training, support and the children waiting nearest to you.
